findings.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36-38` + `app/models/post.rb:128-132` — unsanitized raw HTML from RSS feeds is rendered directly to all forum viewers.** `TopicEmbed.import` is called with `i.content` straight from the feed (only `CGI.unescapeHTML` applied), stored via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` for that mode returns `raw` verbatim — bypassing the normal cook/sanitization pipeline entirely. Unlike `import_remote` (which restricts tags/attributes via `Readability::Document.new(..., tags: [...], attributes: [...])`), the RSS path has no whitelist. Any attacker who can influence the configured feed (compromised feed source, MITM on `feed_polling_url`, or a malicious admin-supplied feed) can inject `<script>`, `<iframe>`, event handlers, etc., which will be served as-is (stored XSS) to every visitor of the imported topic, including within the embeddable-host's own domain via the embed iframe. Fix: run RSS-sourced `contents` through the same tag/attribute whitelist used in `import_remote` (or a dedicated HTML sanitizer) before persisting, regardless of import path.

**`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:22-28` — referer-based access control is trivially bypassable.** `ensure_embeddable` relies solely on `request.referer`, which is client-supplied and can be omitted or spoofed by any direct HTTP client (browsers won't fake it via JS, but curl/proxies can). This is the only gate before enqueueing retrieval/rendering of arbitrary `embed_url` content. It's a reasonable first line of defense for the common case (blocking cross-site iframe embedding), but should not be treated as the sole security boundary — worth a comment noting this is best-effort, and consider combining with the existing `X-Frame-Options` + host-match on `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (which is solid) as the real enforcement point rather than relying on referer for authorization decisions beyond UI framing.

**`app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-32` — race condition can raise an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`.** Between the `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` check and `TopicEmbed.create!`, two concurrent jobs (e.g., overlapping `PollFeed` runs or a `PollFeed` + `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` racing on the same URL) can both see `embed.blank? == true` and both attempt `create!` against the unique index on `embed_url`, causing the second to raise and abort the job/transaction ungracefully. Wrap the create in a rescue for `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or use `find_or_create_by`/upsert) and fall back to the update path.

**`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15` — origin check is not exact.** `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` only confirms `e.origin` is a substring of `discourseUrl`, not that it equals the expected origin. It's not the classic reversed/spoofable form, but it's still a fragile string-match rather than an exact `===` comparison, and could accept unintended origins if `discourseUrl` ever contains extra path/query segments. Prefer `e.origin === discourseUrl` (normalized to just scheme+host+port).
`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:34` — trailing double blank line before `end`; stray style nit from what looks like a generated stub.
`lib/topic_retriever.rb:55` — file is missing a trailing newline.
`spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2` — `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` appears unrelated to this spec (likely copy-paste leftover); unused requires add noise.
`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:1` — `require_dependency 'email/sender'` doesn't appear to be used anywhere in the file; looks like a leftover import.

`lib/topic_retriever.rb#invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`, not scheme — `https://` vs `http://` for the same host both pass. Likely intentional/harmless given `embeddable_host` is a bare host string, but worth a comment confirming that's deliberate.

No i18n or UI messaging is shown to the end user when `import_remote`/`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` fails (e.g., unreachable host, non-HTML content, timeout) — the `loading` view will spin indefinitely with no error/timeout affordance in `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`/`embed.js`. Consider a timeout + user-facing failure state.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36-38` + `app/models/post.rb:128-132` — unsanitized raw HTML from RSS feeds is rendered directly to all forum viewers.** `TopicEmbed.import` is called with `i.content` straight from the feed (only `CGI.unescapeHTML` applied), stored via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, and `Post#cook` for that mode returns `raw` verbatim — bypassing the normal cook/sanitization pipeline entirely. Any attacker who can influence the configured feed (compromised feed source, MITM on `feed_polling_url`, or a malicious admin-supplied feed) can inject `<script>`, `<iframe>`, event handlers, etc., which will be served as-is (stored XSS) to every visitor of the imported topic, including within the embeddable-host's own domain via the embed iframe. adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, RSS item HTML is taken from `i.content` and only passed through `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `String#scrub` (which does not sanitize tags/attributes). That `content` is then persisted via `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The diff also changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` verbatim when `cook_method` is `:raw_html`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Therefore, RSS-sourced HTML can be stored and later rendered as-is (e.g., via `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`, and likely anywhere else that displays `cooked`), enabling stored XSS if the feed content is attacker-controlled/compromised. Unlike `import_remote`, the RSS path has no tag/attribute whitelist.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic check-then-insert: `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` followed later (inside a transaction) by `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. Because `topic_embeds.embed_url` has a unique index (added in `CreateTopicEmbeds`), two concurrent executions for the same URL can both observe `embed.blank?` and then both attempt `create!`; the second will raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/handling in this method or the calling jobs/controllers shown, so the exception will bubble and abort the job/request path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `lib/topic_retriever.rb#invalid_host?` compares only `URI(@embed_url).host`, not scheme — `https://` vs `http://` for the same host both pass. Likely intentional/harmless given `embeddable_host` is a bare host string, but worth a comment confirming that's deliberate.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `invalid_host?` intentionally validates only the host: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. Since `embeddable_host` is configured as a bare host string (see `config/site_settings.yml`), the code has no way to express/require a specific scheme. Allowing both `http` and `https` for the same host is therefore expected behavior, not a verifiable bug/security defect introduced by this diff. The proposed finding is more of a commentary/suggestion than a real problem.

Consider a timeout + user-facing failure state.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: when `EmbedController#best` can’t find an existing `TopicEmbed`, it always renders `embed/loading` and enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`. The loading view just reloads every 30s with no failure state. In the job path (`TopicRetriever#fetch_http` → `TopicEmbed.import_remote` → `open(url).read` / `Readability::Document.new(...)`), there is no error handling for network/timeout/invalid content exceptions, so the job can fail and no `TopicEmbed` will ever be created. In that case, subsequent reloads keep hitting the same branch (topic_id still nil) and the UI remains stuck on “Loading Discussion...” indefinitely, with no user-visible error/timeout affordance in `loading.html.erb`/`embed.js`.
